A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SPARK and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. The original experiments and code listings can be matched reliably despite additions and relocation in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original SPARK evaluations on CLRS, component ablations, five-seed search trajectories, and evolved architecture examples, including appendix results for 30 tasks.

after.justification: v3 retains the original empirical results and adds scope-control experiments and evaluations on five non-CLRS benchmarks.

M1.justification: The ASR–RC–SAR procedure, OPERATOR/ACTION regions, feasibility checks, and archive-based search remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 and all six program listings are retained. The new execution example and additional evaluations do not document a changed method.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluations on MNIST-1D, 20News, CartPole-v1, Mice Protein Expression, and Breast Cancer Wisconsin, substantially extending coverage beyond algorithmic reasoning. All 30 CLRS tasks were already present in v1's Table A.1; their increased prominence is not new coverage.

E2.justification: Table A.2 adds a focused comparison with diagnostic methods such as Random-Scope SAR, Fixed-OP SAR, and Fixed-ACT SAR. The main external comparator set—OpenEvolve, EvoPrompting, FunSearch, and EoH—remains unchanged; reusing these methods on additional benchmarks does not itself expand that set.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce four MNIST-1D backbone configurations, classification accuracy/loss and reinforcement-learning return metrics, and search-cost measurements. Table A.5 specifies 100 proposed candidates for OpenEvolve, EvoPrompting, and SPARK versus 400 for EoH and FunSearch. These are additional protocols; the existing CLRS search-and-transfer protocol is retained.

E4.justification: Appendix A.4 substantially expands the ablations to test whether region tags alone suffice, whether random or fixed scope selection works, and whether RC directives provide additional benefit. These controls extend the earlier ASR-versus-RC+SAR comparison. Existing search-dynamics analyses and evolution traces remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same five-seed trajectories with means and min–max shading in Figure A.1. v3 adds no new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests for its additional result tables.

E6.justification: Original CLRS table values and plotted results are unchanged. New results include MNIST-1D average accuracy of 95.99% for SPARK versus 70.25% for OpenEvolve, and DFS accuracy of 50.27% for Random-Scope SAR versus 80.50% for full SPARK. v3 also reports full-suite means and replaces the erroneous 18-task conclusion summary with 21/30 and 19/30 wins, consistent with the retained Table A.1.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(4), the factor-local feasible-set definition, and the heuristic feasibility argument remain unchanged. Appendix A.3 explains metric bookkeeping without adding mathematical results, substantive derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The central factor-isolated editing contribution and DFS headline results remain. v3 corrects and emphasizes the full-suite CLRS contribution, qualifies comparable compute as model-level MACs, and adds a conclusion that SPARK improves or matches OpenEvolve across five additional benchmarks.

C2.justification: The new Limitations section explicitly acknowledges transfer failures on BFS, Floyd–Warshall, and KMP, additional search-time LLM costs, and dependence on manually defined factors. Appendix A.4 interprets the new controls as evidence that tags alone are insufficient. These additions substantially strengthen qualifications and mechanism interpretation.

D1.justification: v3 adds a SPARK code-repository link, cost-accounting definitions, and wall-clock and per-candidate training times in Table A.5. These improve access information and resource disclosure, while the existing pseudocode and listings remain unchanged. Detailed training and implementation recipes for the new benchmarks are still sparse.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting the five new benchmarks and removes peripheral citations previously attached to appendix interpretations, including Fu et al. (2019) and Qi et al. (2026). The related-work discussion and positioning relative to NAS, iterative refinement, and structured editing remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 revises experimental summaries, clarifies terminology, corrects CC to SCC, updates authorship and publication text, and adds Limitations and Acknowledgement sections. The appendix receives clearer subsection organization, but most existing prose, the main narrative sequence, and code listings are retained.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the tabular presentation with main-text Table 2 and appendix Tables A.2–A.5, covering controls, an execution example, benchmark scores, and costs. Existing algorithms and Figure 2 are repositioned, and the former Table 2 becomes Table 3. The original figure images and code-listing displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Table A.2 directly tests whether tags alone explain SPARK's gains, substantially strengthening evidence for the central mechanism beyond v1's limited component ablation. Broader evaluations and explicit cost, transfer, and factorization limitations improve validation and transparency. New-benchmark protocols and uncertainty remain underreported, and Table A.4's Base and EoH averages disagree with its displayed scores. These weaknesses limit precision but do not outweigh the substantial gains in experimental support and qualification.
